R4D-bear-atv-0002.name: By Timber Creek
R4D-bear-atv-0002.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R4D-bear-atv-0002.parkWhat: where the truck road ends (Enterprise Creek One FSR); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2021 (5 years old), 120 m W: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2021 (fire N51724), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
W facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Timber Creek 30 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

flags.t: Region 4: it is unlawful to feed or bait deer, elk, moose and other hoofed game, or turkeys, anywhere in the Kootenay Region (synopsis page 37, 99%). Snowmobiles may not be used for hunting in Region 4 from 1 April to 30 November (page 37, 99%).

seasonRows.notes: bag 2; private land only, with landowner permission

plan: Drive: from Village of Nakusp, about 81 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Hwy 6 (E Hwy 6), Hwy 6, Hwy 6 (Union St), Enterprise Creek FSR.
Park: 49.81039, -117.28147, where the truck road ends (Enterprise Creek One FSR); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle). Map links below.
Ride: 5.5 km on Enterprise Creek One FSR, Enterprise Creek Two FSR, Section_One, Section_One_A by ATV (all terrain vehicle) or 4x4 on rough road, estimate. Then walk 220 m S, climb about 1 m.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 4-17, Region 4. No baiting in Region 4. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R4D-bear-atv-0002.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 4-17: about 188 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.11 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.2 km and about 1 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).

R4D-deer-drive-0003.name: 370 m SE of Slocan Lake
R4D-deer-drive-0003.pressureWhy: Busier: within 1 km of a paved road (estimate).

evidence.t: Mule deer winter range u-4-001 unit 139 (official), right here. Counts from October.
Cutblock harvested 2007 (19 years old), 740 m SE.
Burn from 2022 (fire N51415, 10 ha), 1.0 km SW.
NW facing slope, 19 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Private fields 490 m NE: deer feed on field edges (fields are private).

flags.t: Private land 490 m NE: no shooting within 100 m (109 yd) of an occupied house or farm building (synopsis page 10, 99%).
Hwy 6 30 m SE: no hunting or shooting on or across the road allowance of a numbered highway or 2 lane public road, 15 m (16 yd) each side of the centre line (synopsis page 10, 99%).

Region 4: it is unlawful to feed or bait deer, elk, moose and other hoofed game, or turkeys, anywhere in the Kootenay Region (synopsis page 37, 99%). Snowmobiles may not be used for hunting in Region 4 from 1 April to 30 November (page 37, 99%).
